IBM.rationale: IBM presents a moderately attractive setup driven primarily by a significant valuation disconnect. The PE has compressed to 22.4x (near the 1-year floor of 19.0x) while trailing profitability metrics have surged to window highs (ROE 32.5%, net margin 15.6%), driven by the Q1 2026 earnings step-up. YoY revenue growth of +9.5% and operating cash flow growth of +18.3% confirm the improvement is broad-based. However, conviction is tempered by: (1) only three quarters of available data — TTM is n/a and durability of the earnings step-up cannot be confirmed; (2) the GAAP-to-non-GAAP EPS gap ($1.28 vs $1.91) means the 22.4x GAAP PE may overstate cheapness if acquisition amortization is the driver — the economic PE on operating earnings is lower, but the true recurring earnings level is uncertain; (3) elevated leverage (liabilities/equity 3.72x, LT debt $57.7B) in a rising-rate environment (10Y at 4.57%, Baa at 6.16%) creates refinancing risk; (4) consulting weakness (signings -15.6%, federal contract cancellations) and below-peer growth (9.46% vs 12.43% peer average) constrain the growth narrative. The CHIPS Act quantum foundry award ($1B) and FedRAMP authorization are directionally positive but unlikely to materially alter near-term fundamentals. The Q1 2026 operating margin of 8.7% vs Q2 2025's 15.3% suggests meaningful seasonality, and the elevated trailing ROE/margins may compress as the z17 mainframe cycle normalizes. Net: valuation appears overdone to the downside relative to observed earnings improvement, but balance-sheet leverage, rate sensitivity, and earnings durability uncertainty cap the score at mildly attractive rather than strongly attractive.
